name: Specialty MEP (cold storage, data center power, labs, commercial kitchens, medical gas)

items.name: Cold-storage refrigeration system (per SF of refrigerated floor area)

cost.method: Low/high = e1 refrigeration line ($30–$90/SF). Cross-check e2: refrigeration = 25–35% of a $175–$275/SF frozen facility = $44–$96/SF. Mid = $55, near the overlap of e1 and the lower half of e2 (cooler space sits at the low end, freezer at the high end).

items.notes: Packaged or central (NH3 / CO2 / HFC) plant, evaporators, piping and controls. Excludes insulated envelope (see freezer-insulated-envelope) and sub-slab heat (see freezer-subslab-heating). Coolers (+34°F) toward low; freezers (−10°F) toward high; blast freezing above range.

items.name: Insulated metal panel (IMP) cold-storage envelope (per SF of panel area)

cost.method: e3 supply-and-install IMP $12–$35/SF, freezer walls (5–6 in, R-40–48) $18–$30/SF, ceiling panels $14–$28/SF (e4); e1 IMPs $15–$40/SF. Low = $15 (cooler-grade panels, both sources' overlap); high = $35 (top of e3 and within e1); mid = $24 = midpoint of the freezer-wall range in e3.

items.notes: Priced per SF of wall + ceiling panel surface, not floor area. A box-shaped freezer has roughly 1.6–2.2 SF of panel per SF of floor (judgment, depends on clear height). Includes panels, trims, sealants; excludes doors (budget $8k–$25k+ per opening per e1) and the slab.

items.name: Freezer floor: sub-slab heating, insulation and vapor barrier package (per SF of freezer floor)

cost.method: e5 sub-slab heating $8–$12/SF; e1 underslab heating and slab package $5–$15/SF for freezer areas. Low = $8 (heating alone, e5), high = $15 (e1 package incl. insulation/vapor layers), mid = $11.

items.notes: Only for areas held below freezing (frost-heave protection). Structural slab itself is in the building shell.

items.name: Data center MEP (electrical + mechanical) per kW of critical IT load

cost.method: Bottom-up: e6 mechanical $2–4M/MW + e7 electrical $3–5M/MW = $5,000–$9,000/kW (2026 US avg, total $11.3M/MW). Top-down: T&T US$12.9–13.3/W (e9 New Jersey, e8 Silicon Valley, 2025) × MEP share 70–87% (e10: electrical 48–54% + mechanical 22–33%) = ≈$9,000–$11,600/kW in high-cost markets. Low = $5,000 (e6+e7 low), high = $11,500 (T&T × upper share), mid = $8,000 = between the bottom-up midpoint ($7,000) and the high-market top-down midpoint (~$10,000). 2025 and 2026 evidence mixed (gap ≤1 yr), expressed in 2026 dollars.

items.notes: Air-cooled, Tier III-ish, 2N/N+1 power. Includes switchgear, UPS, generators, PDUs/busway, cooling plant and CRAH/CRAC. Excludes shell, sitework, utility substation/interconnection, land and IT equipment. Liquid-cooled / AI halls run ~7–10% higher per T&T methodology notes. Do not stack with emergency-generator or ups-system for the same load.

items.name: Permanent standby / emergency generator, installed (per kW)

cost.method: e11 (NJ OEM, 2014): $450–$650/kW for a permanent emergency generator incl. transfer switch and wiring of critical loads; e12 (DoD microgrid study via CleanTechnica, 2012): $300–$600/kW for 100+ kW gen-sets. Expressed in 2014 dollars (anchor e11); e12 is 2012 dollars and was used only to set the low end. Mid = $550 = midpoint of e11. High extended to $750 for sound-attenuated enclosure, sub-base fuel tank and longer feeder runs. The build script escalates from 2014; generator equipment prices have risen faster than general construction since 2021, so verify current quotes.

items.notes: Diesel or natural gas, ~100 kW–1 MW, incl. ATS. Large units (1 MW+) trend lower per kW, small (<100 kW) higher. Not for data centers when data-center-mep is used.

items.name: UPS system with batteries, installed (per kW)

cost.method: No clean public UPS-only $/kW found. Derived as a share of data-center electrical cost: e7 electrical $3,000–$5,000/kW; UPS modules + batteries + bypass taken as ~20–30% of that electrical package (judgment) ≈ $600–$1,500/kW, mid $1,000. Applies to N capacity with 5–15 min battery; 2N doubles.

items.notes: Three-phase double-conversion UPS, batteries (VRLA or Li-ion), maintenance bypass, installation. Lithium-ion carries an initial premium. Do not add when data-center-mep is used.

items.name: Laboratory HVAC premium over office HVAC (per SF of lab area)

cost.method: Derived (no public source fetched). Office HVAC ≈ $30–$45/SF vs. wet-lab HVAC ≈ $90–$150/SF (once-through 100% outside air, 6–10 ACH, fume hood exhaust, energy recovery, tighter controls) — judgment based on typical cost-consultant elemental ratios of lab vs. office MEP. Premium = difference ≈ $45–$110/SF, mid $70.

items.notes: Add on top of a shell + standard-TI budget when converting office to wet lab. Dry lab / tech space toward low; vivarium or high fume-hood density above high. Excludes lab casework and fume hoods themselves (Division 11/12).

items.name: Commercial kitchen equipment package, installed (per SF of kitchen area)

cost.method: Derived (no public source fetched). Typical full-service restaurant cooking line, prep, dish and storage equipment package ≈ $150k–$400k for a 1,500–2,000 SF back-of-house (judgment from franchise-style equipment budgets) ≈ $100–$250/SF, mid $160. Quick-service/fast-casual lines toward low; hotel/banquet or scratch kitchens toward high.

items.notes: Equipment, stainless tables/shelving, dish machine, smallwares rough-in and setting. Excludes hood/exhaust (kitchen-hood-system), walk-ins (walk-in-cooler), grease interceptor and the building MEP rough-in.

items.name: Type I kitchen hood system incl. fire suppression, exhaust fan, make-up air and grease duct (per LF of hood)

cost.method: Derived (no public source fetched). A 12–16 LF Type I hood with wet-chemical suppression, upblast exhaust fan, tempered make-up air unit and welded grease duct to roof typically totals ≈ $25k–$70k installed (judgment) ≈ $1,500–$4,500 per LF of hood, mid $2,800. Short duct runs/untempered MUA toward low; multi-story grease duct shafts or tempered MUA toward high.

items.notes: Per linear foot of hood canopy. Includes hood, Ansul-type suppression, exhaust fan, MUA, grease duct and controls.

items.name: Medical gas & vacuum systems per operating room (incl. allocated source equipment)

cost.method: Derived (no public source fetched). Per OR: O2/N2O/medical air/vacuum/WAGD/N2 outlets, zone valve box, area alarm and piping ≈ $25k–$50k; plus allocated share of manifolds, med-air compressor and vacuum pump plant in a 2–6 OR ambulatory surgery center ≈ $15k–$100k per OR (judgment). Total ≈ $40k–$150k, mid $75k.

items.notes: Excludes ceiling booms/equipment management systems (FF&E/medical equipment). Hospitals spread source plant over many more outlets; use the low end per OR plus building-wide medical gas allowance.

items.name: In-ground grease interceptor, 1,000–1,500 gal precast, installed

cost.method: Derived (no public source fetched). Precast concrete tank ≈ $5k–$12k delivered plus excavation, traffic-rated lids, inlet/outlet piping, sampling port and restoration ≈ $10k–$30k (judgment). Total ≈ $15k–$45k, mid $25k. Large (2,500+ gal) or deep/dewatering installs exceed the high.

items.notes: Per interceptor. Under-sink hydromechanical traps are far cheaper ($1k–$5k) and not covered here.

items.name: Walk-in cooler or freezer box with refrigeration (≈ 8×10 to 10×12), installed

cost.method: Derived. Box: 8×10×8 ft ≈ 450 SF of panel; prefab walk-in panels run below site-built IMP (e4 freezer walls $18–$30/SF) at ≈ $10–$25/SF ≈ $5k–$11k; plus condensing unit/evaporator, door, floor and electrical ≈ $7k–$24k (judgment). Total ≈ $12k–$35k, mid $20k. Freezers toward high.

items.notes: Restaurant/retail walk-in. Remote condensing units, combo cooler/freezer boxes or boxes >150 SF exceed the high.
